patients.summary: Math teacher with ADPKD who joins on hemodialysis in 2018, receives a deceased donor kidney in December 2020, and then works through acute and chronic rejection, CMV colitis, Pneumocystis pneumonia, DKA and, in 2026, EBV-positive polymorphic PTLD treated with reduced immunosuppression and rituximab. Insulin-treated type 2 diabetes and hypertension run through the whole chart.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

43 yo man joining us; last PCP retired this summer. Polycystic kidney disease is the headline: kidneys failed and he started in-center hemodialysis about a year and a half ago, three mornings a week. Listed at the regional transplant center for a deceased donor kidney. Left native kidney was removed in 2011 for an infected cyst; right native kidney still in. Teaching full time (HS math) and determined to keep doing it.

DM2 on basal/bolus insulin, glargine 24 u qhs and lispro by a 1:12 carb ratio. Checks fingersticks before meals. Denies lows. HTN on amlodipine 10. Aspirin 81.

PMH: ADPKD, ESRD on HD, DM2, HTN
PSH: L native nephrectomy 2011 (infected cyst)
Meds: amlodipine 10 daily, ASA 81, glargine 24 u qhs, lispro 1 u/12 g carb with meals
Allergies: NKDA
FH: father with PKD, on dialysis in his 50s, died at 58 of a ruptured brain aneurysm. Mother HTN and DM2. Sister has PKD and is on hemodialysis now.
SH: smokes cigarettes daily, has tried to stop before. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. Lives in South Hadley.

ROS: tired on dialysis days, otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing. BP as recorded. HEENT nl. Neck supple, no LAD. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, fullness R flank, nontender. Ext no edema. Feet: intact skin, pulses 2+, monofilament sensation intact. Skin no rashes.

A/P
1. ADPKD / ESRD on HD, transplant listed - nephrology and dialysis unit drive this. Requested their records and the transplant center's listing letter.
2. DM2 on insulin - A1c today (knowing it reads a bit unreliable with dialysis anemia). Eye exam due.
3. HTN - on amlodipine 10, BP okay for a dialysis day off.
4. Tobacco - smoking affects his transplant candidacy, he knows. Talked through quitting, counseling offered; he wants to set his own date. Will revisit each visit.
5. HM: Tdap today. HCV, HIV, HBsAg/Ab today. Flu and pneumococcal next month; hep B series if not immune. PHQ-2 0.

RTC 3 months.

documents.author: transplant surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRANSPLANT CENTER - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/24/2020, discharged 12/29/2020.

Procedure 12/24/2020: deceased donor kidney transplant, graft placed in the left iliac fossa with ureteroneocystostomy and ureteral stent. Native right polycystic kidney left in situ (left native removed 2011).

Course: prompt graft function, no dialysis needed after surgery. Creatinine down to 1.1 by discharge. Stent to come out in clinic at about 4 weeks.

Discharge medications:
- tacrolimus 5 mg PO BID, trough goal 8-10 ng/mL
- mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg PO BID
- prednisone 5 mg daily (after steroid taper)
- trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole SS 1 tab daily (PJP prophylaxis x 6 months)
- amlodipine 10 mg daily
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- insulin glargine 24 units qhs; insulin lispro 1 unit/12 g carbohydrate with meals
Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: transplant clinic twice weekly with labs for the first month. Hemodialysis discontinued; dialysis unit notified.

events.reason: decreased urine output and edema two weeks after kidney transplant

reports.text: Specimen: transplant kidney, percutaneous needle core biopsy. Two cores with adequate cortex. Interstitial mononuclear cell infiltrate with tubulitis and tubular epithelial injury. Glomeruli and arteries without significant abnormality. C4d immunostain negative.
reports.conclusion: Acute T-cell-mediated rejection of the renal allograft.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology discharge summary
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
TRANSPLANT NEPHROLOGY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 1/7/2021, discharge 1/12/2021.

Reason: 45M, deceased donor renal transplant 12/24/2020 for ADPKD, readmitted about two weeks out with falling urine output, fatigue and new swelling of both legs.

On arrival BP 160/95, T 37.2 C. Mild bilateral leg edema; graft in the LLQ tender to palpation. Creatinine 3.2 (discharge baseline 1.1), BUN 46, K 5.8. UA: 1+ protein, WBC casts on microscopy.

Graft biopsy 1/8: interstitial mononuclear infiltrate with tubular injury, read as acute T-cell-mediated rejection.

Treatment: IV methylprednisolone pulse daily x3, then resumed prednisone 5 mg daily. Tacrolimus level 8.9, dose unchanged. Hyperkalemia managed with dietary restriction and binder in hospital; K normal by day 3. Urine output recovered; creatinine falling at discharge.

Discharge meds unchanged from transplant discharge. Allergies NKDA.
Problems: acute rejection (treated), hyperkalemia (resolved), ADPKD, DM2, HTN.
Follow-up: transplant clinic in 3 days with labs.

Transplant clinic labs yesterday: creatinine down to 1.2 per their portal (he read it to me). Making good urine, legs no longer swollen. Sugars ran 250-300 on the pulses, back to 140-190 now; took extra lispro per ratio, no lows.

Meds reconciled against transplant discharge: tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, pred 5, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24 qhs, lispro ratio. NKDA.

A/P: rejection treated, graft function back near baseline - transplant nephrology following closely. Hyperkalemia resolved. DM - steroid bump resolved, no change. Out of work on leave until transplant team clears him. COVID vaccine: transplant team wants him to get it when eligible; he's on the list. In-person visit in 6-8 weeks.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD

CC: R flank pain, blood in urine.
HPI: 45M with ADPKD, deceased donor kidney 10 weeks ago (graft LLQ), on tacrolimus/MMF/prednisone. Two days of escalating right flank pain and urine that turned red today. Also a dull frontal headache since this morning. No fever, no dysuria. FH notable for kidney disease - father on dialysis in his 50s.

Meds per pt list: tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24, lispro. NKDA.

Exam: BP 160/100. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. Large firm right flank mass, tender. Graft site nontender. Neuro nonfocal.

UA: blood and protein; microscopy RBC present without casts.
Renal US: large cysts throughout the right native kidney; transplant looks normal, no hydro.
MRI brain (headache, family hx of ruptured aneurysm): 4 mm ACom saccular aneurysm, no bleed.

MDM: hematuria and flank pain most consistent with a bleed into a native-kidney cyst in ADPKD; graft not involved, creatinine at his baseline. Unruptured intracranial aneurysm, incidental to a benign-feeling headache that improved here with acetaminophen.

Dispo: home. Acetaminophen for pain, no NSAIDs. Hydrate. Return for fever, clots, retention, worst headache or neuro change. Genetic testing for ADPKD sent after discussion with transplant nephrology on call. Referral placed to neurovascular surgery. PCP f/u this week.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit - post ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit since transplant. Seen in ED 3/1 for R flank pain and bloody urine - felt to be a bleeding cyst in the old right kidney. Urine cleared by the next afternoon, pain now a 2/10 ache, acetaminophen twice yesterday. Headache gone.

The bigger worry for him is the aneurysm on the MRI - his dad died of one at 58. Spent most of the visit on this. Explained what 4 mm means and that it hasn't bled; the decision about watching vs treating belongs with neurovascular surgery and he should hear it from them. I made sure the referral is moving; ED placed one too, consolidating.

Exam: BP improved from ED, as charted. R flank full, mildly tender. Graft nontender. Neuro intact.

A/P:
1. Unruptured ACom aneurysm - neurovascular referral. BP control matters; amlodipine 10 continued. He is already off cigarettes.
2. Native cyst hemorrhage, resolved - acetaminophen only.
3. Transplant - followed by transplant nephrology; genetics pending.
Return precautions for thunderclap headache reviewed. Back to teaching next week.

documents.title: Neurovascular surgery consultation
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
NEUROVASCULAR SURGERY - CONSULTATION

Thank you for referring Mr. Murphy, 45, with ADPKD and a recent kidney transplant, for an incidentally found aneurysm.

Imaging reviewed: 4 mm saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery, unruptured, regular contour.

History: father with polycystic kidney disease died of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm at 58. Former smoker, quit December 2019. Hypertension on amlodipine. NKDA.

Exam: alert, fluent, cranial nerves intact, strength and coordination normal.

Discussion: we talked at length about endovascular or open treatment versus surveillance. Family history and ADPKD raise his risk; the small size, regular shape and his recent transplant (with procedural and anesthetic risks while still early on immunosuppression) favor watching for now. After discussion he prefers surveillance.

Plan: MRA (non-contrast time-of-flight) in 6 months, then yearly if unchanged. Blood pressure control and continued tobacco abstinence. Seek emergency care for sudden severe headache. We will revisit treatment if it grows or changes shape.

documents.title: Bloody diarrhea, vomiting
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called before school. A week of crampy belly pain, vomiting on and off, and now diarrhea with blood several times a day. No travel, nobody sick at home. Transplant recipient 3.5 months out on MMF/tac/pred.
This needs a same-day transplant evaluation, not a school day. Advised he call the transplant coordinator now and go to the transplant center ED if he can't be seen today; if lightheaded or bleeding heavier, 911. He agreed. I left a message for the transplant coordinator as well.

documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY INPATIENT SERVICE - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 4/12/2021, discharged 4/19/2021.

45M, ADPKD, deceased donor kidney 12/2020 complicated by early acute rejection, recent native-cyst hematuria. One week of abdominal pain, emesis and bloody stools. Denied travel or sick contacts.

Admission: afebrile, BP 130/85, HR 88. Abdomen diffusely tender, no rebound or guarding.
Labs: Hgb 12.1, WBC 9.0 with normal differential, plt 250, Cr 1.2 (his post-transplant baseline), LFTs normal. CMV PCR 185,000 IU/mL.

Colonoscopy 4/13: multiple large, shallow ulcers through the colon, biopsied. Pathology: CMV inclusions, CMV immunostain positive.

Dx: CMV colitis in a kidney transplant recipient.

Treatment: IV ganciclovir (renally dosed) 4/13-4/18 with resolution of bleeding and tolerance of diet, transitioned to oral valganciclovir 900 mg BID. Immunosuppression continued per transplant nephrology. Tacrolimus level in range.

Discharge meds: valganciclovir 900 mg BID (NEW), tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24 qhs, lispro per ratio. NKDA.

Follow-up: weekly CMV PCR and CBC via transplant clinic; duration of valganciclovir per transplant ID/nephrology once viral load is undetectable.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 3 days after discharge for CMV colitis. Stools formed, no blood since 4/16. Eating normally. Tired. Taking valganciclovir 900 BID - pharmacy needed a PA for the quantity, which our office and the transplant center both submitted; approved yesterday.

Meds reconciled; valganciclovir added. NKDA.
Exam: looks tired, afebrile. Abd soft, minimal LLQ tenderness near graft? he says that's the colon, no different from before. No edema.

A/P: CMV colitis on treatment - transplant team checking PCR weekly. Watch counts on valganciclovir (their labs). Genetic test from the ED still pending. Neurovascular plan noted (MRA in Sept). He is not back at school yet. RTC 1 month, sooner prn.

TRANSPLANT NEPHROLOGY CLINIC
Visit 4/28/2021

Dear colleague,

I saw Joel today, four months after his deceased donor kidney transplant for ADPKD-related end-stage kidney disease, and two weeks after discharge for CMV colitis. He has no complaints and reports taking every dose of tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone. Valganciclovir continuing.

BP 132/86. Exam unremarkable; graft nontender.

Labs: creatinine 2.8 mg/dL, up from his 1.2 baseline at the time of the CMV admission. BUN 44. Urinalysis without protein or blood. Tacrolimus trough 8.4, in range.

Genetic testing (sent from the ED in March) returned: heterozygous pathogenic variant in PKD1, consistent with his clinical ADPKD. Genetic counseling information given for his family.

We will see him back with labs.

Medication list: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, valganciclovir 900 mg BID, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg, insulin glargine 24 units, insulin lispro per ratio. NKDA.

Transplant Nephrology

reports.conclusion: Chronic active T-cell-mediated rejection with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy.

TRANSPLANT NEPHROLOGY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 5/12/2021 (via ED), discharge 5/17/2021.

Presentation: malaise, falling urine output, mild graft tenderness, no fever. BP 158/98. Firm, slightly enlarged allograft. Creatinine 3.9. Duplex ultrasound normal vessels and perfusion, no obstruction.

Biopsy 5/13: chronic active T-cell-mediated rejection with IFTA. C4d negative.

Treatment: IV methylprednisolone pulses, then prednisone back to 5 mg daily; tacrolimus continued with trough 8-10 goal (8.7 on admission). Creatinine improving at discharge.

CMV PCR not detected on admission; valganciclovir course completed and stopped at discharge per transplant ID.

Discharge meds: tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24, lispro per ratio. Valganciclovir STOPPED. NKDA.

Third admission since the transplant. Biopsy showed chronic rejection; steroid pulses again. Discouraged today - asked whether the kidney will last. Told him honestly that transplant nephrology is the right team to answer that, and that his creatinine has been coming down at every check since the biopsy.

Glucose ran high on the pulses, now settling. Off valganciclovir. Bowels normal.

Exam: BP as charted. No edema. Graft mildly tender.

PULMONARY MEDICINE - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 1/12/2022, discharged 1/22/2022.

46M, ADPKD, deceased donor kidney 12/2020 with prior acute rejection, CMV colitis 2021. Two weeks of progressive breathlessness, nonproductive cough and low-grade fevers. Off PJP prophylaxis since 6/2021.

Arrival: afebrile, RR 28, SpO2 92% on room air. Diffuse crackles both lungs.
Labs: WBC 6.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250, creatinine 1.5 (baseline 1.3), LDH 450 (ref 140-280). SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative.
CXR: bilateral interstitial infiltrates.
Induced sputum: routine stains and cultures negative for bacterial, viral and fungal pathogens.
Bronchoscopy with BAL 1/13: Pneumocystis jirovecii identified by direct immunofluorescence.

Dx: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

Course: treatment-dose TMP-SMX, supplemental O2 by nasal cannula, weaned to room air by day 6. Creatinine back to 1.3. Tacrolimus monitored.

Discharge meds: TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs TID through 2/1/2022 (21 days), then TMP-SMX SS 1 tab daily lifelong; tacrolimus 5 BID; mycophenolate 750 BID; prednisone 5; amlodipine 10; ASA 81; glargine 24; lispro per ratio. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within a week, transplant clinic 2 weeks.

MEDICAL ICU / HOSPITAL MEDICINE - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 7/5/2022 via ED to the ICU; transferred to the floor 7/7; discharged 7/9/2022.

46M with ADPKD, deceased donor kidney transplant with prior allograft rejection, insulin-treated type 2 diabetes. Two days of breathlessness, urinating constantly and very thirsty. Told us he had not been taking his insulin as prescribed in recent weeks.

ED: BP 130/85, HR 110, T 37.2 C. Deep, rapid respirations. Skin warm and dry.
Labs: glucose 480, HCO3 12, arterial pH 7.20, K 5.2, Na 140, Cl 95 (anion gap 33), BUN 28, Cr 1.2. Urine ketones positive. A1c 11.4.

Dx: diabetic ketoacidosis, precipitated by missed insulin.

Course: IV fluids and insulin infusion per DKA protocol with potassium monitoring; gap closed overnight, transitioned to subcutaneous glargine and lispro. Creatinine stable. Diabetes educator saw him twice. Tacrolimus continued.

Discharge meds: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro 1 unit/12 g carbohydrate with meals plus correction, tacrolimus 5 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10, ASA 81. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week.

Seen 3 days after discharge for DKA. He was candid: since spring he'd been taking glargine some nights and lispro hardly ever, partly burnout after a year of hospitalizations, partly a meter that died and he never replaced. The DKA scared him.

Now: taking glargine 24 nightly and lispro with meals per ratio since discharge. Fingersticks 140-210 on the new meter. No vomiting, eating and drinking normally.

Exam: well-appearing, normal breathing. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. DKA, resolved - BMP today to confirm bicarb and K. Insulin as before; new meter and strips sent. Glucose log by portal weekly for a month.
2. DM2, A1c 11.4 - agreed plan: alarms on his phone, pen in his school bag. Educator follow-up booked.
3. Burnout - not depressed by PHQ-2 (0), but tired of being a patient. We talked about what makes the routine sustainable.
RTC 3 months with A1c; sooner if numbers stay above 250.

orders.reason: fevers, weight loss, cervical lymphadenopathy in a transplant recipient

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit - acute
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 3 weeks of tiredness that is not getting better over break, fevers on and off, mostly evenings, and he's down 5 lb without trying. Noticed lumps on both sides of his neck a week ago. No cough, dyspnea, diarrhea, urinary symptoms. No sick contacts he knows of.

O: Weight down as charted. Afebrile in clinic. Bilateral cervical lymph nodes, firm, mobile, nontender. Liver edge palpable below the costal margin; spleen tip felt on inspiration. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Graft nontender. Skin no rash.

A/P: B symptoms with bilateral cervical adenopathy and organomegaly in a 5-year kidney transplant recipient on tacrolimus/MMF/prednisone - PTLD needs to be excluded first, infection second. CBC/CMP today. Called the transplant nephrologist on call - they agree, and hematology/oncology at the transplant center will see him next week; urgent referral placed. Fever precautions: if >101 persistently, rigors, or short of breath, go to the transplant ED.

Addendum 1/7: WBC up and new anemia, as resulted. Forwarded to heme/onc with the referral.

reports.text: Specimen: lymph node, right cervical, excisional biopsy. Lymph node with effaced architecture by a polymorphic proliferation of small and intermediate lymphocytes, immunoblasts and numerous plasma cells. Immunohistochemistry: CD20 positive B cells; EBV-encoded RNA (EBER) in situ hybridization positive in many cells. No sheets of monomorphic large cells to suggest a monomorphic lymphoma.
reports.conclusion: Polymorphic post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder, EBV-positive (EBER+), CD20 positive.

documents.title: Hematology/oncology consultation
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - NEW CONSULTATION (seen 1/14/2026; addended with pathology 1/20)

Reason: fevers, fatigue and lymphadenopathy in a kidney transplant recipient.

HPI: 50M with ADPKD, deceased donor renal transplant 12/2020, maintained on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone; history of CMV colitis and Pneumocystis pneumonia. Three weeks of fatigue, intermittent fevers and a 5-lb weight loss.

Meds: tacrolimus 5 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, insulin glargine 24, lispro. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.3 C. Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Mild hepatosplenomegaly. No other palpable adenopathy.

Labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 10.5, plt 150, creatinine 1.2 (his post-transplant baseline), LDH 450 (ref 140-280), EBV PCR 98,000 copies/mL.

Procedure: excisional biopsy of a right cervical node performed 1/16 by surgical oncology.

Pathology (1/20): polymorphic lymphoid proliferation with numerous plasma cells; CD20 positive; EBER positive.

Impression: EBV-associated polymorphic post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder.

Plan: staging CT chest/abdomen/pelvis. Joint plan with transplant nephrology to follow.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Enlarged bilateral lower cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes at the thoracic inlet, right larger than left. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Lungs clear without nodules or consolidation. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral lower cervical/supraclavicular adenopathy. No intrathoracic disease.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Liver mildly enlarged without focal lesion. Spleen mildly enlarged without focal lesion. No retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic adenopathy. Right native kidney enlarged with multiple cysts; left native kidney absent. Transplant kidney in the left iliac fossa enhances normally without hydronephrosis or peritransplant collection. Bowel unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Mild hepatosplenomegaly without focal lesions. No abdominal or pelvic adenopathy. Polycystic right native kidney; unremarkable renal transplant.

documents.body: Staging CT reviewed: disease limited to neck/supraclavicular nodes plus mildly enlarged liver and spleen; nothing in chest or abdomen otherwise. Heme/onc meeting with him Friday.

documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY - TREATMENT PLANNING VISIT 1/23/2026 (with transplant nephrology)

Diagnosis: polymorphic EBV-positive, CD20-positive PTLD. Staging CT: bilateral lower cervical/supraclavicular nodes, mild hepatosplenomegaly, no other sites.

Plan, agreed with transplant nephrology and the patient:
1. Reduce immunosuppression: STOP mycophenolate today. Tacrolimus reduced from 5 mg BID to 3 mg BID, new trough goal 4-6 ng/mL. Prednisone 5 mg daily continues.
2. Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly x 4, starting 1/29/2026, at our infusion center with premedication.
3. EBV PCR, CBC, creatinine and tacrolimus level weekly during treatment; graft surveillance by transplant nephrology given the rejection history.
4. Restaging CT about 8 weeks after the last dose.

Continue TMP-SMX SS daily. Avoid live vaccines. He will take a leave from teaching through the infusions.

documents.title: Hematology/oncology follow-up
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Hematology & Oncology 5/5/2026. Polymorphic EBV+ PTLD after reduction of immunosuppression and 4 weekly doses of rituximab. Asymptomatic, weight recovering. No palpable adenopathy or organomegaly.
Restaging CT 4/27: resolution of adenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly. EBV PCR not detected. LDH 196, normal.
Assessment: complete response.
Plan: surveillance visits every 3 months for the first year with exam, CBC, LDH and EBV PCR. Immunosuppression stays at the reduced level (tacrolimus 3 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, no mycophenolate) per transplant nephrology.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels like himself again. Weight back to baseline. Finished the school year full time. Heme/onc called it a complete response in May.
Sugars stable. BP fine on amlodipine.
Exam: no LAD, no organomegaly. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema. Feet intact.
Meds: tacrolimus 3 mg BID, pred 5, TMP-SMX SS, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24, lispro ratio. No MMF.
A/P: DM2/HTN stable; A1c, BMP, ACR. PTLD in remission - per heme/onc q3 months. RTC Sept.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology clinic letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Transplant Nephrology 7/14/2026. Six months after reduction of immunosuppression for PTLD, now in complete response. Creatinine around 1.3, a little above his old 1.2 baseline but stable. Tacrolimus trough 5.6 on 3 mg BID, at goal. No mycophenolate. Prednisone 5 mg. Continue; labs monthly, visit in 3 months.

documents.title: Hematology/oncology surveillance
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body: Hematology & Oncology 8/10/2026 - PTLD surveillance. Feels well, no fevers or sweats, weight back up. No adenopathy or organomegaly. CBC normal, LDH 182, EBV PCR not detected, creatinine 1.3. Remains in complete response. Next visit November.
